metaDescription: Monitor CPU, memory, disk, network and battery on your Mac. Manage the native macOS charge limit and check optional AI usage limits.
heading: Your Mac, at a glance.
description: CPU, memory, battery and AI usage limits in one native Mac app.
notFoundDescription: The page you’re looking for doesn’t exist or has moved.
heroTitle: See what your Mac is doing.
heroLead: A native menu bar app for CPU, memory, disk, network, sensors and AI plan limits, with the macOS charge limit one click away.
releasePending: The public release is being prepared. Follow releases on GitHub.
featuresTitle: Your whole Mac, one click away
featuresLead: Click the menu bar icon or press ⌥⌘M. Readings refresh every few seconds while the popover is open and slow down when it’s closed.
cpuDescription: Load, performance and efficiency cores, frequency and the busiest processes.
memoryDescription: Used memory, pressure and swap, with a notification when pressure stays high.
diskDescription: Free space and live read and write speed.
networkDescription: Download and upload speed for the active connection, with history.
sensorsDescription: CPU, GPU, SSD and battery temperatures and fan speed, where your Mac reports them.
processesDescription: Apps using the most CPU and memory, grouped by app or by process.
batteryTitle: Keep the battery at 80%, without thinking about it
batteryLead: Monny uses the charge limit built into macOS, the same setting as in Battery Settings. No helper, no root access.
batteryCheck2: Stays on when Monny is closed
batteryDetail2: macOS keeps it through sleep and restarts
batteryDetail3: In Monny or in System Settings → Battery
batteryRequirement: Needs a Mac with a battery and macOS 26.4 or later. 100% turns the limit off.
aiTitle: AI plan limits next to CPU and memory
aiLead: See how much of your Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Grok plan is left before you start a long task. Monny reads the limits with each tool’s own sign-in on this Mac.
aiNote: Turn it on in Settings. Monny doesn’t store or refresh those sign-ins and sends them only to each tool’s own service.
dashboardLead: History from 1 minute to 7 days, top processes and temperature sensors in one window.
privacyLead: A system monitor sees a lot. Monny keeps all of it on your Mac.
localDescription: No account, analytics or telemetry. The only network requests are update checks and the AI limits you turn on.
noHelperDescription: The charge limit uses the setting built into macOS and changes it with your regular user permissions.
nativeDescription: Built with SwiftUI for macOS 26. One shared sampler refreshes only what you’re looking at.
openSourceDescription: MIT licensed. Read the code, build it yourself or report an issue on GitHub.
installLead: Monny is free. Public DMG releases will be available on GitHub.
installDetail2: Open the DMG and drag the icon
installDetail3: Once for each download, see below
noticeInline: Not notarized yet: the first launch needs one extra step.
noticeTitle: Monny isn’t notarized by Apple yet
noticeDescription: Notarization needs a paid Apple Developer ID, which the project doesn’t have yet. Monny is signed and its code is open, but on first launch macOS says it can’t verify the app. You only need to allow it once, using either option.
noticeQuote: “Apple could not verify “Monny” is free of malware…”
pasteCommand: Paste the command and press Return.
settingsStep1: Try opening Monny once, then dismiss the warning.
settingsStep3: Scroll to Security, choose Open Anyway and confirm.
noticeFootnote: Needed once for each download. Only allow a copy you downloaded from this project.
questionsLead: Something else? Open an issue or start a discussion on GitHub.
faqQ1: Why does macOS say it can’t verify Monny?
faqA1: macOS skips this warning only for notarized apps. Monny is signed and open source but isn’t notarized yet. Allow your downloaded copy once using either option in the installation guide above.
faqA2: Macs with Apple silicon running macOS 26 or later. The charge limit also needs a Mac with a battery and macOS 26.4 or later. Intel Macs aren’t supported.
faqQ3: Does Monny send my data anywhere?
faqA3: Readings stay on your Mac. Monny connects only for update checks and, if you enable AI limits, requests to Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor and xAI using each tool’s own sign-in.
faqQ4: Will the charge limit stay on after I quit Monny?
faqA4: Yes. macOS keeps its own limit after you quit Monny, through sleep and restarts. You can also change it in System Settings → Battery.
faqA5: Monny checks for signed updates with Sparkle and asks before installing them. You can turn automatic checks on or off and check manually in Settings.
faqA6: Yes. Monny is free and open source under the MIT license. No account, subscription or ads.
ctaTitle: Give your Mac a closer look
ctaLead: Free and open source. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.
